text: Anxiety when travelling alone, especially in small hotel rooms. I booked rooms with windows for years. A few panic attacks in the first months.
Nichts Bleibendes, eher großer Respekt vor der Natur.

The retreat brought the birth trauma back with full force, and with a new layer: the belief that my daughter had died. For weeks after, I had moments where I looked at her and felt she wasn't real, that she was a dream. I'd hold her very tight and smell her hair to convince myself. I had panic attacks almost daily. I had flashbacks to the operating table, now mixed with the retreat, the mat, the hands holding me down.

I couldn't let my husband take her out alone because I was terrified something would happen. I didn't sleep well. I lost weight. I felt I was going crazy and was ashamed because I'd gone to the retreat voluntarily. My husband was supportive but frightened.

After about six months it got gradually better, but the anxiety is still higher than before the retreat.

For about a year I had obsessive thoughts that I might have hurt someone without knowing. I'd check the news after going out, retrace my route in my head, sometimes even go back to check. My doctor said it sounded like OCD. It came on after the trip and I'd never had it before. It's much better now but still comes back when I'm stressed.
Ich hatte ein halbes Jahr lang Angst, Zug zu fahren. Auch bei Fahrkartenkontrollen hatte ich Herzrasen. Mittlerweile ist es besser.

Since that night I've had chronic depersonalisation and derealisation. It's been two and a half years. I often feel like I'm not fully in my body, like part of me is still floating somewhere. Looking in the mirror is strange. The world often looks flat and dreamlike. I also feel emotionally numb, like the feelings are behind glass. My breakup, which I was trying to escape from, still hurt, but in a weird, muted way.

I've been depressed most of the time since. Not because of the breakup anymore, but because I feel I've lost my connection to myself. I've had times where I didn't see the point of going on like this. I don't enjoy things the way I used to. I play guitar and it feels mechanical now.

I have a lot of anxiety about the DP, I check myself all the time, and sometimes I have panic attacks where I'm afraid I'll 'leave' my body completely again. I can't sleep on my back because that's how I was lying that night.

I couldn't watch the news for a long time, and still avoid live coverage of any disaster. Whenever I hear sirens or helicopters I feel a jolt of fear. For about six months I had anxiety and a recurring nightmare of being in the basement while the world ends. I also became quite obsessive about emergency preparedness and kept a bag packed by the door, which my friends teased me about.

Strangely, I also feel that the experience gave me a deep sense of how connected we all are, and how much suffering there is in the world. I'm more compassionate now, I think.
Ich hatte danach Angst vor Übelkeit und Erbrechen und habe einige Wochen sehr schlecht gegessen. Die Schlangenbilder kamen nachts manchmal wieder. Nach ein paar Monaten war es vorbei.

For about a week after, the world looked wrong, too sharp, too bright, a bit cartoonish. Then that faded but I had insomnia for months. I'd lie in bed with my body buzzing like during the trip. I also became afraid of anything that might keep me awake, like caffeine. I'd panic at night if I couldn't fall asleep, thinking I'd be stuck awake forever.

The voices faded within a day, but I've been terrified of developing schizophrenia ever since. I monitor my thoughts constantly. I had a few months of anxiety and depression. No more voices, thankfully.
Relationship with my parents was strained for a year. I felt a lot of shame. Some anxiety at parties.
